label: early original-phase input of w/u/v (and d)
explanation: Token detector for the letters w, u, v (and weakly d, n) while the original sequence is being read, gated by position: it fires mostly in the first ~5 original steps and fades for later positions. 97% of activation mass is in the original phase. Activation rate and mass rank w (52% rate, 42% of mass) > u > v > d > n; x and m fire rarely, and other tokens, digits, the delimiter and the copy phase almost never fire (copy phase holds 2.6% of mass, mostly w inputs). The largest activations (about 0.4) come from w at steps 2-3 when preceded by v/w, so a run of w/v/u inputs strengthens it. Misses are mostly late-position w/u inputs and n inputs; false positives are d/v/u at steps 2-4 that stay below threshold.

issues: Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.820, R 0.796, F1 0.808, MR 0.897. The phase shares (original 97.4%, copy 2.6%), the token rates (w 52% > u 38% > v 32% > d 21% > n 9.5%, with x and m rare) and the copy-phase mass sitting almost entirely on w inputs all check out.

The unit is really a token-strength x position gradient, not a hard cutoff. At t=0, w, u, v and d fire 100% of the time and n 0%. Precision then falls with t at a rate that depends on the token: for w it is 1.0/1.0/0.97/0.92/0.82/0.60/0.34 over t=0..6, and for d it is 1.0/0.63/0.44/0.32/0.16. The predicate's per-token cutoffs are a fair way to cut this gradient, and the explanation's description of the fading matches it.

Systematic gap: the effect of the previous token is much stronger than 'a run of w/v/u seems to make it stronger' suggests, and the predicate ignores it. When the previous input is in {w,u,v,d,n}, firing is close to certain even for weak tokens or later positions. d at t=2 fires 99% of the time after a w/u/v and 33% otherwise; n at t=1 fires 100% after a w/u/v/d/n and 23-60% otherwise; u at t=4 fires 99% after a w/u/v and 55% when no w/u/v came before. Many of the missed activations are n inputs, or later w/u/v inputs, that follow a token from this family.

The fix is modest. Adding 'family token following a family token, t<7' raises test F1 from 0.808 to 0.820 and mass recall from 0.897 to 0.935. Adding copy-phase w inputs lowers F1 to 0.761 because precision drops, so leaving the copy phase out is the right call.
The label leaves n out even though the explanation mentions it. That is minor: n never fires at t=0 and fires mostly after another family token.
skeptic.revised_label: original-phase input of w/u/v/d/n, strongest early and decaying with position (w slowest to decay); kept alive at later positions when the previous input is also one of these letters
